title: Director of Customer Success

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: For a global technology company with 1,100+ employees serving customers in 40+ countries, customer retention, satisfaction scores, and post-sale support efficiency are critical KPIs. This role owns the customer experience after equipment purchase, including addressing performance issues, warranty claims, technical support escalations, and ensuring customers achieve their ROI. Durst's customers in outdoor signage and vehicle wraps frequently face challenges with premature fading, UV damage, and graphics degradation—issues that generate support tickets, erode customer satisfaction, and damage Durst's reputation for reliability. By recommending Tedlar as a best-practice protective solution, Customer Success can proactively reduce complaint volume, lower warranty claim rates, and position Durst as a trusted advisor who helps customers maximize their equipment investment. This role cares about NPS scores, support ticket reduction, customer churn prevention, and demonstrating measurable value to existing accounts. Tedlar's 12-20+ year durability, UV protection, and graffiti resistance directly address the most common pain points their customers face in outdoor applications, making it a tool to improve customer outcomes, reduce support costs, and increase account retention—all while strengthening Durst's consultative positioning in the market.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: The Director of Customer Success at Durst owns post-sale customer experience across their global installed base of large-format printing systems. Their scope includes managing support operations, tracking warranty claims, monitoring customer satisfaction metrics (NPS, CSAT), reducing churn, and ensuring customers successfully achieve ROI on their P5 series and other printer investments. They likely report to a VP of Customer Operations or Chief Customer Officer and manage teams of technical support specialists, customer success managers, and training professionals. While they don't directly purchase materials like Tedlar, they have significant influence over recommended best practices, application guidelines, and ecosystem partner solutions that Durst suggests to customers. Their recommendations shape what materials Durst certifies, trains on, and includes in customer success playbooks.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Tedlar's protective films directly address the most common post-sale pain points this role faces with Durst's outdoor application customers. For sign manufacturers using Durst printers to produce outdoor billboards and signage, Tedlar overlaminates prevent the UV fading and cracking complaints that generate support tickets. For vehicle wrap installers printing on Durst equipment, Tedlar's graffiti resistance solves vandalism issues that lead to warranty claims and customer dissatisfaction. For architectural graphics customers, Tedlar's extreme temperature range and weather resistance eliminate premature failure issues that damage Durst's reputation for reliability. By recommending Tedlar as a certified protective solution, Customer Success can proactively reduce the volume of degradation-related complaints, lower warranty claim processing costs, and position Durst as a trusted advisor who helps customers maximize equipment value through proper material selection.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role is measured on customer retention rates, Net Promoter Score, support ticket volume and resolution time, warranty claim frequency and cost, customer churn reduction, and account expansion opportunities. Their personal success depends on keeping Durst's global customer base satisfied, productive, and renewing contracts. When customers experience premature graphic failures due to inadequate protective films, it creates support escalations that consume team resources, erode customer trust, and threaten renewals. Tedlar provides a proactive solution: by integrating it into customer onboarding materials, application best practices, and success playbooks, they can prevent problems before they occur. This reduces reactive support demands, improves satisfaction scores, and positions Customer Success as a strategic value-add function rather than just a cost center. Additionally, successful customers who achieve superior outdoor performance become case studies and references that support new customer acquisition—creating cross-functional value that elevates this role's impact.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Durst's recent product launches (P5 X in late 2024, P5 SMP at DRUPA 2024) mean new customers are onboarding and establishing material workflows—creating a window to introduce Tedlar as a recommended best practice before habits are set. Their Platinum sponsorship and presence at PRINTING United Expo 2025 (just completed) and ISA Expo 2024 indicate they're actively acquiring new customers in outdoor signage and graphics segments where protective film selection is critical. The company's eleven 2025 PRINTING United Alliance Pinnacle Awards demonstrate their reputation for quality is currently strong—making this an ideal time to introduce solutions that protect and extend that reputation. Additionally, with global operations in 40+ countries, any improvements to customer success processes can scale rapidly across their installed base, creating immediate operational impact. This is the right moment to engage before Q2 planning cycles begin and while customer onboarding processes are being refined for new product lines.

personalization_hooks.hook: Durst's customers in outdoor signage and vehicle wraps commonly face UV degradation and fading issues that generate support tickets and warranty claims
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging the challenge of supporting customers whose outdoor graphics fail prematurely despite using quality Durst printing equipment. Position Tedlar as a proactive solution that Customer Success can recommend to prevent these issues before they reach the support queue, reducing reactive workload and improving satisfaction scores.

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent P5 X and P5 SMP launches mean new customers are establishing material workflows and application best practices right now
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame this as a timely opportunity to integrate Tedlar into onboarding materials and customer success playbooks for new product lines. Suggest a brief conversation about how other printer manufacturers have reduced support costs by certifying protective films as part of their recommended application workflows.

personalization_hooks.hook: Durst positions itself on reliability and performance, but downstream material failures can undermine that brand promise regardless of printer quality
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Connect Tedlar to Durst's brand positioning by emphasizing how protective film selection affects the total customer outcome. Position the conversation as strategic: how can Customer Success help customers achieve the full reliability and performance Durst promises by recommending materials that match the equipment's quality level?

recommended_approach: Lead with the operational pain point of support tickets and warranty claims related to outdoor graphic failures. Frame Tedlar as a preventative tool that reduces reactive support demands and improves customer outcomes, rather than leading with product specs. This role cares most about reducing workload, improving satisfaction metrics, and enabling customers to succeed—so position Tedlar as a customer success enabler, not a sales pitch.
